item.title: db Group to cover the 400 annual contribution for its TCN employees
item.description: db Group has become the latest company in Malta to pledge support for its third-country national employees after Budget 2027 introduced a new 400 annual infrastructure contribution for non-EU workers. The group said it will cover the full charge for eligible existing and new TCN employees, with existing staff covered when it falls due on work permit renewals from 1 April 2027. Workers whose permits expire before the end of March must apply on time to qualify, and employees must still pay their own permit application fees, including the 800 fee where applicable. The company will also cover the new 83 monthly driving licence charge for eligible staff.

item.title: Dalli tells COP31 climate action must not burden families and businesses
item.description: Environment Minister Miriam Dalli told the COP31 climate summit in Antalya that climate action must translate into investment strengthening resilience without placing an excessive burden on people. Co-leading the EUs negotiations on climate change adaptation, she said Malta is already feeling rising temperatures and extreme weather and must have a seat where decisions are taken. A draft deal from co-host Australia removed all references to fossil fuels but included a target to electrify the global economy, with nearly 200 nations seeking a consensus agreement by Friday.

item.title: Maltese man appears in court over €153m fuel fraud as Spain seeks extradition
item.description: Maltese police arrested one of two Maltese nationals suspected of involvement in a €153 million fuel fraud scheme in Spain on a European Arrest Warrant. Rodrick Grech, 45, from Naxxar, appeared in Valletta court on Thursday, where he refused to consent to extradition, leaving the decision to a judge. His defence did not contest the warrants validity but requested bail. The arrest followed a co-ordinated international operation into a network accused of laundering €153 million between 2021 and 2024.

item.title: Labour says leaked PN statute would weaken party due diligence and narrow leadership
item.description: Labour presented a leaked draft revision of the Nationalist Party statute at a press conference on Thursday, saying it would cut the party leadership committee from seven members to four and exempt MPs running for party leader or deputy leader from due diligence checks. Ministers Jonathan Attard and Glenn Bedingfield said the document carried tracked changes attributed to PN general secretary Charles Bonello and came from party members unhappy with Alex Borgs leadership. The Nationalist Party has disputed the documents authenticity, calling it a doctored version of its existing statute.

item.title: European Commission calls on Malta to stop finch trapping
item.description: The European Commission told Malta on Thursday to stop allowing finch trapping, saying its research scheme for seven protected finch species breaches EU bird protection rules. In a Reasoned Opinion it accused Malta of using a research derogation to continue recreational trapping despite two EU court rulings, and gave the country two months to respond. The government said it would continue talks, defend the research exemption and protect Maltas cultural traditions, with the case potentially going before the EU Court of Justice if the response is unsatisfactory.

item.title: Archbishops Curia backs Green Ribbon campaign for non-EU workers
item.description: The Archbishops Curia said it is supporting the week-long Green Ribbon campaign highlighting the challenges faced by third-country nationals in Malta, distributing the ribbon among staff as a gesture of solidarity. The campaign is organised by the TCN Alliance Malta, Solidarjet, Moviment Graffitti and TCNs United, and comes after budget measures including a new 400 annual infrastructure contribution on work permits and the withdrawal of free public transport and childcare. TCN Alliance Malta said the campaign is intended as a peaceful but undeniable confrontation with the policies that caused the impasse.

item.title: Convicted Qormi drug trafficker given probation order instead of jail
item.description: Renald Baldacchino, 38, known as il-Garru, was given a three-year probation order after being convicted of supplying cocaine and heroin from a Qormi garage, drug possession, firearms offences and breaching a suspended sentence. The court took into account his successful completion of a drug rehabilitation programme. The case stems from a March 2018 police raid in which nine people were arrested and officers seized cash, two firearms and drug paraphernalia, with 26 grams of cocaine found at roughly 18 per cent purity.

item.title: Malta records the highest share of air and sea travel in the EU
item.description: Eurostat data for 2025 show Malta had the largest share of trips made by air in the EU at 61.6 per cent, more than three and a half times the EU average of 17.2 per cent, with Cyprus second at 51.1 per cent. Malta also topped the EU for waterway travel at 38.4 per cent, ahead of Greece at 15.9 per cent and Finland at 6.9 per cent. Across the EU, residents made 1.2 billion trips in 2025, with 81.4 per cent by land, and cars the most used mode of transport at 63.3 per cent.

item.title: MEIA clarifies artists income proposal as a temporary pilot scheme
item.description: The Malta Entertainment Industry and Arts Association said a permanent wage for all artists falls outside the scope of its proposal, clarifying that it had recommended a small pilot running for a limited period with clear rules and independent evaluation. The clarification follows the Nationalist Partys backing of the proposal for a basic wage for artists, and comes amid an online debate to which MEIA said it contributed no part.

item.title: PN raises concerns over delays in specialist training for doctors
item.description: The Nationalist Party said delays in specialist training forced the Medical Association of Malta to order industrial action, with doctors who applied on 15 May still awaiting start dates six months later. PN spokesperson Stephen Spiteri said the health service is struggling to meet growing demand and that more doctors would allow patients to be seen sooner. MAM registered a trade dispute on 12 November over delays in appointing junior doctors to basic specialist trainee posts, and its directives take effect on 20 November.

item.title: Services turnover edged up, with working-day adjusted index 10.1 per cent higher year on year
item.description: National statistics show seasonally adjusted services turnover rising 0.9 per cent against the previous quarter, while working-day adjusted turnover in selected service activities was 10.1 per cent higher than a year earlier. The strongest quarterly growth was recorded in real estate activities at 19 per cent, followed by transportation and storage at 6.9 per cent and motor vehicle trade at 4 per cent. Turnover declined in professional, scientific and technical activities, wholesale trade and administrative and support services, while employment, gross wages and hours worked all increased.

item.title: Abela inaugurates €50 million St George’s Mall investment in St Julian’s
item.description: Prime Minister Robert Abela inaugurated the €50 million St George’s Mall commercial development in St Julian’s, part of the wider db Group project at St George’s Bay that also includes the Hard Rock Hotel Malta and ORA Residences. The mall spans some 15,000 square metres over two floors and houses around 60 retail and food and beverage establishments, including 18 brands opening in Malta for the first time, plus 1,267 parking spaces. Abela said the Maltese economy has reached a stage where it can take “the next leap forward”, with the investment intended to create better jobs, skills and earnings in hospitality and commerce.

item.description: The Pharmacy of Your Choice scheme, which distributes free medicines to entitled patients, has been extended to 234 community pharmacies across Malta and Gozo. The pilot, launched in December 2007 in Imġarr and Għargħur, lets patients collect medicines from a pharmacy of their choice instead of public hospital pharmacies.

item.title: PAC opens scrutiny of Enemalta over the 2023 power cuts
item.description: Parliament's Public Accounts Committee started on Wednesday examining the National Audit Office report into the widespread power outages Malta experienced in the summer of 2023. The PAC's examination focuses on Enemalta's handling of the outages and will take evidence as part of the audit process. The hearing puts the utility's preparedness and network performance during the heatwave under parliamentary scrutiny.

item.description: Speaker Carmelo Abela ruled that comments by former Malta Employers Association director general Joseph Farrugia against Labour MP Nigel Vella did not constitute a prima facie breach of parliamentary privilege, while urging greater respect in public discourse. The dispute followed Farrugia returning the Ġie ir-Repubblika honour in protest over Yorgen Fenech's acquittal in the Daphne Caruana Galizia murder case.

He said prosecutor recruitment since 2022 covered only five entry-level posts and 55 trainee lawyers, that the Deputy Attorney General post has been vacant for three years, and criticised the Attorney General's lack of criminal-law background.

Income tax generated around €3.4 billion in 2025, equal to 51% of government revenue from taxation.

item.title: Mayors seek full-time option in five-point local government resolution
item.description: Malta's and Gozo's mayors approved a five-point resolution calling for local government reform, including the option for mayors to serve full-time and a larger say in how funding for local councils is allocated. The resolution was adopted at the Local Councils Association's annual mayors conference in Gozo on 13 and 14 November.

The resolution was adopted at the Local Councils Association's annual mayors conference in Gozo on 13 and 14 November.

item.title: Carabott questions sustainability of Malta's €12 billion public debt
item.description: Nationalist MP Darren Carabott questioned Finance Minister Clyde Caruana on Malta's public debt, which he put at around €12 billion, arguing that borrowing is being used for consumption and wages rather than investment. Caruana defended the sustainability of public finances, noting that recurrent and wage spending is covered by revenue while capital spending is not fully covered.

The regulator reported 273.5 kilos of legal cannabis sold in 2024 and 2,170 CHRA members, mostly aged between 31 and 40.

item.title: Maltese suspect in €153m Spanish fuel fraud arrested on European Arrest Warrant
item.description: One of two Maltese nationals suspected of involvement in a €153 million fuel fraud scheme in Spain has been arrested by Maltese police on a European Arrest Warrant. Spain is seeking the surrender of the 45-year-old suspect from Naxxar to face proceedings. The arrest follows a co-ordinated international investigation, and comes as Maltese authorities separately said two Maltese men are under investigation over the same alleged fraud.
